readme.text:
**The deterministic trust layer for DeepSeek Harness — nine guards, one dashboard, one command.**

为 DeepSeek Harness 打造的确定性信任层：九个守卫 + 一块人话面板，一条命令全装上。

[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-trust-suite)
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-trust-suite)
[](LICENSE)
[](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/dsh-trust-suite/commits/main)
[](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-trust-suite
```

Nine deterministic guards watch what a DSH agent **reads, writes, executes, spends, and remembers** — plus a plain-language [dashboard](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/dsh-trust-panel) and a [guardian pet](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/dsh-guardian-pet) that makes the state visible at a glance. Every decision is made by pure rule engines: **zero LLM calls in the trust path**, ~140 unit tests, verified against real DSH sessions.

| Guard | Watches | Acts at | Mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| [dsh-read-guard](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/dsh-read-guard) | what the agent **reads** | `tools/post-execute` | wrap (default) · observe · block |
| [dsh-pr-gate](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/dsh-pr-gate) | what the agent **writes** | `tools/pre-execute` | deny before write |
| [dsh-egress-gate](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/dsh-egress-gate) | where data **goes** | `tools/pre-execute` | web: deny · shell: observe |
| [dsh-attest-chain](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/dsh-attest-chain) | what **happened** (evidence) | `tools/result` | sign + hash chain |
| [dsh-mcp-test](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/dsh-mcp-test) | which **tools exist** | `tools/change` | baseline diff |
| [dsh-prompt-drift](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/dsh-prompt-drift) | the **system prompt** | `system-prompt/assemble` | baseline diff |
| [dsh-freeze](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/dsh-freeze) | the **plugin composition** | startup | fingerprint pin |
| [dsh-compaction-guard](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/dsh-compaction-guard) | what compaction **forgot** | `session/event` | report + ledger |
| [dsh-janitor](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang

Plus two consumers of the same event stream:

- [**dsh-trust-panel**](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/dsh-trust-panel) — a sidebar dashboard that translates the nine channels into plain language, bilingual (zh/en), with a status light and acknowledge flow.
- [**dsh-guardian-pet**](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/dsh-guardian-pet) — the same state as a creature: it dozes while all is clear, bristles when something is caught, and writes you a weekly battle report.

```mermaid flowchart LR A["tool call"] --> B{"pre-execute
pr-gate · egress-gate"} B -- deny --> X["blocked"] B -- allow --> C["execute"]

```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-trust-suite ``` That single bundle installs all nine guards plus the dashboard. Prefer git checkouts? `./install.sh web` from this repo does the same from GitHub sources (everything ships prebuilt `lib/`, no `allowBuilds` approval needed). Individual guards are also installable on their own.

> [!WARNING]
> **This is a policy-check and audit toolset, not a sandbox.** The guards make deterministic decisions at DSH's plugin hook points; they are not OS-level network controls, filesystem permissions, or a semantic guarantee that "the model was never influenced". Hard boundaries belong to the host sandbox, system permissions, or a proxy — layer this suite *on top of* those, not instead of them.

What each guard actually does, stated plainly:

- **Detect** (report + ledger): mcp-test, prompt-drift, freeze, compaction-guard, janitor flag drift and leftovers — they do not block anything.
- **Enforce before the fact**: pr-gate denies out-of-scope file writes; egress-gate denies non-allowlisted web destinations (shell fetches are observe-only by default).
- **Mutate results**: read-guard wraps flagged content in a quarantine envelope (default) or blocks it — in wrap mode the original text is still in context, explicitly marked untrusted.
- **Record**: attest-chain appends a signed, hash-chained evidence record per tool result.
Known boundaries are documented per guard in each repo's README — coverage limits, default-off modes, and trust-on-first-use for baselines.

**Does this call any LLM?** No. Every decision is a pure rule engine — same input, same verdict, auditable.

**Can I install just one guard?** Yes. Every guard is an independent npm package; the suite is only a convenience bundle. [dsh-trust-panel](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/dsh-trust-panel) even works standalone — its read/egress engines ship inside the panel package.

**Does read-guard delete or rewrite the original file?** Never. It only changes what reaches the model's context, and only for high-severity findings in wrap/block mode.

**Windows?** Yes — CI runs Windows + Linux on Node 20/22/24 for every guard.

**Exact supported set** (as verified): Node ≥ 20 · npm ≥ 11.15 (staged publishing route) · DSH 0.2.x source snapshot 0.2.1-alpha.2 with host packages on the 0.1.2-rc.1 line · dsh plugin add installs via the official profile flow (pnpm). Plain-npm installs of the suite depend on the registry peer graph resolving cleanly — dsh-prompt-drift ≥ 0.1.1 carries the peer fix that makes that resolve.
